chunks: And through it, from Abdullah ibn Jabla, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Sayqal, from his father Mansur, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you wake up and spend the night of a day in which you do not see an Imam from the Family of Muhammad, then love whom you used to love, hate whom you used to hate, and be a friend to whom you used to be a friend, and await the Deliverance morning and evening.
ai.seo_question: What should a believer do on a day when an Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt is not seen?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to maintain their state of love, hatred, and friendship with their respective groups even during a day when an Imam is not visibly present among them, while continuously awaiting the relief (al-Faraj). This teaching emphasizes continuity of social and spiritual bonds during the period of the Imam's absence or occultation, reflecting the Shia concept of 'Intizar' (awaiting) as an active, dynamic state of readiness rather than passive waiting. The emphasis on 'a day' suggests that even brief periods of the Imam's invisibility require sustained vigilance and adherence to the established social hierarchy of the faithful.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (3) Abdullah bin Jibilla narrated from Muhammad bin Mansoor as-Sayqal from his father that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “If you spend a day and a night without finding an imam of Muhammad’s progeny, then still love whom you have loved before, hate whom you have hated before, follow whom you have followed and wait for the deliverance day and night.” The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni from Muhammad bin Yahya from Ahmad bin Muhammad from ibn Fadhdhal from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Attar from Ja’far bin Muhammad from Mansoor from someone from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).
